transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-07-08 14:00 PDT
Duration: ~47 minutes
Attendees: Sophie (Redwood AE), Ethan (Redwood SE), Priya (BlueWave ML), Carlos (BlueWave Infra), Linda (BlueWave Security)

Auto-summary (auto-generated):
- Quick review of last week's benchmark; networking egress issue discovered causing occasional model downloads to fail.
- SE applied a kernel patch that improved batching behavior; basics look better but p95 latency still high under burst load.
- Action items: share network diagram, customer opens firewall ticket, SE to re-run benchmarks.

Topics: networking/firewall, routing & VPC peering, runtime upgrade, KV cache warming, benchmark results, next steps

Transcript:
[00:00] Sophie: okay good afternoon everyone thanks for joining ya we'll kick off in a sec, can everyone hear me?
[00:06] Priya: yes yep loud and clear, thanks Sophie
[00:09] Carlos: good here
[00:11] Ethan: all set
[00:13] Sophie: awesome so agenda quick recap of last week's runs, network follow ups, runtime patch + perf numbers, then next steps. Priya you want to start with any updates from your side?
[00:25] Priya: yeah thanks, so we ran the end-to-end flows this morning using the test harness you gave us. overall ok, but we hit that earlier failure where nodes couldn't download the model artifacts intermittently. looked like an egress restriction on our side or maybe the proxy was blocking larger files, so Carlos is gonna investigate. also saw p95 spikes when we do concurrent chat workloads, so want to understand caching warm up.
[00:48] Carlos: yeah that's right, infra logs show some 403s from the artifact host at 03:12 and again at 03:45, firewall logs show outbound blocked on port 443 when the artifact blob size was >50MB, we have a default proxy that enforces scanning so it might be the chunked transfer. we're opening a ticket with infra security to allow that flow.
[01:10] Linda: quick security note: we'll need the exact endpoints and IP ranges to add to our allowlist, also any cert pinning or mTLS requirements.
[01:22] Sophie: yep understood, we'll send a network diagram with CIDR ranges and required ports. Ethan, quick perf recap?
[01:29] Ethan: sure, um so after applying the kernel/video— sorry kernel scheduling patch (small transcription note, patch to runtime scheduling and attention kernel selection) we saw steady-state throughput improve about 12% on the 8xA100 nodes. baseline tests (no caching) p95 was around 320ms, with patch p95 dropped to ~240ms. with KV prefix cache warmed and batching tuned to 8 requests per batch median latency dropped to ~110ms, p95 ~185ms. but under burst of 200 concurrent users we still see p95 spike up near 420ms, looks like queueing in the request router.
[02:15] Priya: that matches what we saw, once we hit simultaneous long context requests (like 8k tokens) it spikes. are those being routed to the same node? could be uneven shard distribution.
[02:28] Ethan: yes there's a routing policy we used that pins customer to a subset of nodes for isolation. it might be worth testing the relaxed routing policy to spread load— though that relaxes isolation guarantees.
[02:38] Sophie: let's capture tradeoffs: isolation vs throughput. Priya what's your preference— do you need strict single-tenant node pinning now or can we loosen for pilot?
[02:47] Priya: for pilot we can relax to improve perf, but for production we'll require isolation because of PHI concerns. so for the pilot loosen is ok as long as we document behavior.
[02:58] Linda: also we need audit logs for any cross-tenant routing changes, must be visible in console and streamed to our SIEM.
[03:07] Sophie: noted, Redwood console has route logs and we can enable audit streaming — we'll include the config doc.
[03:12] Carlos: quick q on VPC peering — are you using AWS Transit Gateway or simple peering?
[03:18] Ethan: current pilot uses VPC peering for simplicity, but Transit Gateway recommended for multi-account scale. for the pilot peering is fine.
[03:25] Carlos: ok that'll simplify firewall rules. I'll add peering route tables to the ticket.
[03:30] Priya: could you also clarify how model updates are pushed? we saw a restart during a rollout earlier, had an impact on in-flight sessions.
[03:38] Sophie: good call — we do rolling restarts by default but we also support warm rollout with zero-downtime handoff for sessionful workloads; SE can show the config. Ethan, explain the model rollout knob?
[03:46] Ethan: yeah, there's a rollout policy. by default the agent pulls model artifacts and restarts the process; in the private pilot we recommend pre-pulling artifacts to a node-local cache and then flipping traffic via the router — that reduces downtime. we added a pre-pull step in the nightly job; the earlier 403s prevented pre-pull so it forced restart.
[04:06] Priya: ok that explains it. so once egress is fixed pre-pull should make the rollout smooth.
[04:12] Sophie: perfect. on the kernel patch we pushed, any regressions we should know about?
[04:17] Ethan: only minor — a logging verbosity increase we will quiet down. otherwise correctness looked good across the eval set, small differences in tokenizer handling (transcription note: tokenizer -> tokeniser) which didn't affect scores.
[04:32] Carlos: what about KV cache eviction — we noticed sometimes the KV cache isn't re-used across similar requests causing higher compute.
[04:39] Ethan: that's likely due to shard placement and tokenization differences; there's a prefix normalization we can enable which increases cache hits by ~18% in our internal tests. downside is slightly more CPU pre-processing. For pilot that's acceptable.
[04:58] Priya: please enable that on the next run.
[05:02] Ethan: will do.
[05:04] Sophie: ok next — security/compliance checklist Linda? anything else from your side?
[05:09] Linda: yes two things: 1) SSO/SAML integration verification, we tried the test SAML flow and got a login mismatch on the redirect URL, need exact ACS URL. 2) KMS integration for customers who want to bring their key — need docs for key rotation and HSM support.
[05:28] Sophie: we'll share SAML ACS endpoint and a KMS integration doc. Redwood supports BYOK via KMS and HSM options in Private.
[05:36] Linda: great. also retention — what's default log retention and can we send logs to our S3 bucket?
[05:43] Ethan: default is 30 days in the console but you can stream logs to your S3 or SIEM; we'll provide the config and an example CloudFormation snippet.
[05:51] Carlos: quick nit on monitoring — when you say p95 in the console is that single-request token latency or end-to-end? we need clarity for SLA.
[05:59] Sophie: good question, p95 shown in the console is end-to-end serve latency including network inside the VPC; we can also surface per-stage metrics (router queue, runtime exec, kv cache hit) as separate panels.
[06:10] Priya: please add runtime exec time to the dashboard. that's most useful for us.
[06:15] Ethan: done, we will add the panel.
[06:18] Sophie: any blockers on your side for the firewall ticket? Carlos?
[06:21] Carlos: just need the list of endpoints and IP ranges, and confirmation on whether to allow chunked transfers and the user-agent for artifact requests. once we have that I'll put through change control.
[06:33] Sophie: noted we'll include example curl and user-agent.
[06:36] Priya: on the performance re-run — what's the test harness config? we want to reproduce exactly.
[06:41] Ethan: we'll share the harness repo link and the exact test CSV. run is: 100 concurrent users, 8-batch, 64 token avg request, context 2048. SE will attach the exact command.
[06:53] Sophie: ok shifting to timeline — are we still on track to complete pilot acceptance by end of month? Priya?
[06:59] Priya: we are optimistic but the egress/firwall and SAML fixes are blockers; once those are done we can validate in 2-3 runs. so if firewall change is in next 48 hours, likely still on track.
[07:12] Linda: security sign off will wait until we validate SAML ACS and KMS rotation doc; depends on sprint but aim for two weeks.
[07:21] Sophie: understoody. let's capture next steps and owners.
[07:25] [10:00] --- long section of detailed technical back-and-forth and screen share of console, logs and grafana panels (transcription imperfect, some words garbled) ---
[30:02] Ethan: uploaded the preliminary CSV results to the shared drive (link: https://redwood.example.com/pilots/bw/benchmarks) — the patched run is named patch-2027-07-08.csv.
[30:18] Priya: reviewing that now, ok I see p95 drop in many scenarios. can we get the raw traces too?
[30:25] Ethan: yes attaching perf traces separately.
[30:30] Carlos: I have one more question about routing policies and fallback: if a node becomes unhealthy does the router fallback to hosted model variants or another private node? we want to avoid egress to hosted in regulated workloads.
[30:44] Sophie: good point — fallback can be configured; for this pilot we disabled hosted fallback. default is to failover to other private nodes within the same VPC; you can configure cross-region fallback but that remains private. hosted fallback is off for BlueWave.
[30:58] Linda: please confirm that in writing.
[31:02] Sophie: will do.
[31:05] Priya: last thing — are there recommended quantization profiles for A100 that you used in the runs?
[31:12] Ethan: we tested int8 quant on held-out models and saw modest quality delta; recommended profile is q4_0 for latency sensitive flows, q8_0 for highest quality. we'll share the profiles.
[31:24] Priya: ok please add to the shared config repo.
[31:28] Sophie: wrapping up — recap of action items: Sophie to send network diagram and firewall example, Carlos will open ticket, Ethan will re-run patched benchmark and enable prefix normalization, Redwood to share SAML ACS and KMS docs, and SE to add runtime exec panel. timeline target 7/12 for benchmark and docs.
[31:47] Carlos: noted.
[31:49] Linda: noted.
[31:50] Priya: thanks all, that covers it for me.
[31:53] Sophie: great thanks everyone we'll follow up in slack and email.
[31:58] Ethan: thanks.
[32:00] Sophie: meeting adjourned.

End notes:
